summary.headline: LCC Projects Q2 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 886 crore and EBITDA margin widened to over 15.5%, with order book at Rs 8,154 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 886 crore (up 34% YoY), EBITDA Rs 137 crore (up 46%) and PAT Rs 77 crore (up 58%), with H1 revenue of Rs 1,688 crore and H1 EBITDA margin of 15.2%. The company completed its IPO, raising Rs 258 crore via fresh issue, and net worth rose to Rs 1,276 crore. Working capital days rose to 123 from 99 because trade receivables climbed to Rs 674 crore on end-quarter milestone billing, which management says will be realised largely in Q3. Management guided to a 14-15% EBITDA margin for the full year and revenue growth of about 20%.

segments.name: Water sector (irrigation, water supply, WTP, desalination)
segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from water and it will keep water as the core focus. Within water, Jal Jeevan Mission is about 20% of the water-sector book, per management.

segments.name: Other sectors (metro, mining, railway, solar)
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue per management. Q2 non-water share was higher, which management attributed to rain-hit irrigation and water supply work.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs 4,300-4,400 crore, about 20% growth; management expects about 40% of revenue in H1 and 60% in H2.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 14-15% for the year and beyond; management said there is no margin pressure.
Order book target of about Rs 10,000 crore by March 2027 (2.5x expected revenue); management also cited Rs 6,000 crore of inflows for the year and Rs 3,000 crore expected by March.
Working capital days expected to return to 90-100 days by year-end; significant receivable realisation expected in Q3.
Capex of about Rs 50-60 crore a year; Rs 30 crore spent in H1 and Rs 30 crore planned in H2.
Revenue growth of 20% or more targeted for subsequent years.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about Rs 30 crore; H2 plan about Rs 30 crore; sustainable run-rate about Rs 50 crore a year, including about Rs 14-15 crore earmarked from IPO proceeds.
Precast factory started in Ahmedabad; on-site precast facilities installed to reduce labour dependence.
Approximately 12,000 labourers on site versus requirement of 10,000-12,000, per management.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 8,154 crore at 30 September 2026, up from Rs 7,953 crore at 31 March 2026; order book to FY26 revenue 2.21x.
H1 FY27 order inflow Rs 1,641 crore; current L1 positions worth Rs 1,583 crore, with L1 from Gujarat and Rajasthan government expected to convert to work orders within about 20 days.
Tenders bid worth about Rs 12,000 crore across Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh; a further Rs 15,000-20,000 crore of tenders expected before March.

Private sector work comes from large clients (Adani, Reliance, Tata), with awards based on past performance and negotiation rather than L1 alone; one thermal-power water project for a private client (Adani) has started execution.
Management sees opportunities in inter-river linking (about 30 projects identified; work under way on 4-5), data centre water supply, and nuclear power water needs; no data-centre orders in hand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook, and does the Q2 margin include one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Artiba Jadeja said Q2 benefited from profitable projects and project mix, and full-year EBITDA margin is guided at 14-15%. Management described its approach as conservative and said it can achieve better.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and order inflow plan for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Rs 4,300-4,400 crore revenue (about 20% growth) and an order book of about Rs 10,000 crore by March, implying about Rs 3,000-4,000 crore of inflows in H2 once L1 wins are counted.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise to Rs 675 crore and when will they be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Billing is done at month-end after certification, with payment usually in 30-45 days. Milestone billing at end-September led to the spike, and management expects most of it to be realised in October.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the cash balance free to use, and why not repay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash is not entirely free: about Rs 290 crore is fixed deposits pledged as margin for bank guarantees, and IPO proceeds are earmarked for objectives to be used from October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and are mobilisation advances interest-bearing?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 capex was about Rs 30 crore, with a sustainable run-rate of about Rs 50 crore a year. Mobilisation advance was Rs 29 crore at 30 September, mostly interest-free; management avoids interest-bearing advances.

qa_highlights.question: Are commodity price swings covered by contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all contracts carry price escalation linked to WPI, or to a direct rate in some contracts, so cost inflation should not hit margins.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivables of Rs 674 crore and 123 working-capital days need to normalise to 90-100 days in Q3-Q4 as management guided.
Order conversion: Rs 1,583 crore of L1 positions must convert to work orders (management said about 20 days); the H2 inflow target of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore depends on tenders still to be bid.
H2 margin: management expects H2 margin near 13-13.5% if H1's 15.2% holds; the full-year 14-15% range is a conservative guide.
Revenue delivery: H1 revenue of Rs 1,688 crore needs about Rs 2,700 crore in H2 to meet the Rs 4,300-4,400 crore target.
Credit rating: management said the rating is stable A+ and that any bank-rate renegotiation would rest on performance, not a rating upgrade.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin, with management repeatedly describing its approach as conservative. Vague on specific numbers when asked about the one-off nature of Q2 margin and the non-water mix, and reliant on repeated historical patterns (40/60 H1-H2 split) rather than hard guidance.
key_quotes: We will maintain our EBITDA around 14% - 15%.
No, there is no pressure on the margin. Our margin will be stable and we will increase it.
All our contracts are secured and covered by price escalation.

adds.what: Precast factory in Ahmedabad started (on-site precast facilities installed); capacity size not stated

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 4,300-4,400 crore (about 20% growth) backed by an order book of Rs 8,154 crore (2.21x FY26 revenue) and H1 inflow of Rs 1,641 crore, with Rs 1,583 crore of L1 positions pending conversion; no concrete capacity addition sized, and the Rs 6,000-10,000 crore year-end order book target is internally inconsistent.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 15.2% vs 13.8% last year and management guides 14-15% for FY27 with no margin pressure, though H2 margin is expected near 13-13.5%, so expansion is not assured beyond current levels.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Precast factory in Ahmedabad has started but its size is not stated, and capex is a steady Rs 50-60 crore a year with no sized new plant, so meaningful new capacity is not clearly signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue target of Rs 4,300-4,400 crore is about 20% growth, backed by an order book of Rs 8,154 crore (2.21x FY26 revenue) and Rs 1,583 crore of L1 positions pending conversion, but H2 needs about Rs 2,700 crore against H1 Rs 1,688 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and management kept capex at Rs 50-60 crore a year with no new plant named, so a major new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls its guidance conservative and says it can achieve better margins, but H2 margin is guided lower at 13-13.5%, limiting upside to the 14-15% range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue needs about Rs 2,700 crore in H2 after Rs 1,688 crore in H1, receivables of Rs 674 crore must be realised in Q3, and working capital days of 123 must fall to 90-100 by year-end.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed beyond the precast facility, which is a capability rather than a product launch.

rows.label: L1 conversion to work orders
rows.why: Gujarat and Rajasthan government L1 positions worth Rs 1,583 crore are expected to convert to work orders within about 20 days, against H1 inflow of Rs 1,641 crore.

rows.label: Receivable realisation and WC normalisation
rows.why: Trade receivables of Rs 674 crore (from Rs 456 crore) are expected to be realised largely in Q3, with working capital days guided back to 90-100 from 123.

rows.label: Debt reduction from IPO and cash
rows.why: Debt is Rs 885 crore against cash of Rs 535 crore, but about Rs 290 crore is pledged as bank-guarantee margin and IPO proceeds are earmarked for use from October, so repayment is conditional.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Rs 4,300-4,400 crore revenue target, 14-15% margin and order pipeline, but vague on whether Q2 margin included one-offs and on the non-water mix; analysts pressed on receivables of Rs 675 crore and cash that is largely pledged.
